subject: sandbox: a toolchain root is judged where it resolves, and macOS says what it widened
prompt:
A plugin tool that declares network endpoints can silently get wider network access than it declared.

The launch plan a sandbox backend returns for a plugin tool (`PluginToolSpawnPlan` in packages/tool-registry/src/tools/plugin-tools.ts) says in `host_enforcement` how the tool's declared endpoints will be enforced. On macOS, Seatbelt can filter outbound traffic by port but not by host, so a declared `api.example.com:443` can only be enforced as `*:443` — any host on port 443. For such a plan the backend reports `host_enforcement: "port"` plus a note describing the widening; when every declared endpoint can be enforced exactly as written (a loopback endpoint, say), it reports `"host-and-port"`. The plugin tool server currently treats `"port"` as enforced, so a named host runs as the whole port with no opt-in and nothing said — while it refuses a tool whose plan reports `"host-and-port"`, which should simply start.

What should happen:
- Only `host_enforcement: "host-and-port"` counts as enforcing the declared endpoints as written. Anything else (`"port"`, `"all-or-nothing"`, `"none"`) widens what the manifest asked for, and the tool is refused unless the plugin is listed in `[extensions] allowUnsandboxedTools` — the refusal Linux (bubblewrap) already gets.
- The refusal notice keeps its current wording ("… cannot enforce its declared network endpoints", naming `allowUnsandboxedTools`), and it now also carries the plan's enforcement written as `host_enforcement: <value>` (e.g. `host_enforcement: port`) together with the plan's own notes, so the reader sees the widening itself (e.g. "ANY host on port 443").
- When the opt-in is given, the tool starts, and its start notice says the declared endpoints "are NOT enforced as written by <mechanism>" (e.g. "are NOT enforced as written by seatbelt", "… by bubblewrap") and includes `host_enforcement: <value>`. The warning logged for the opt-in should likewise say the access is wider than declared.
- A declaration the backend can enforce as written (`"host-and-port"`) starts with no refusal.

Keep the plugin-tools exports and the plan's shape as they are, and keep the existing tests passing.
